question: Who is known as the ‘Father of Microfinance’? He founded Grameen Bank to make small loans available to the poor.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Muhammad Yunus**__ .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Muhammad Yunus:**

 
 
• **Muhammad Yunus** is known as the **Father of Microfinance** for his pioneering work in providing small loans to the poor.
 
• He founded the **Grameen Bank** in Bangladesh in 1983 to offer microcredit to impoverished individuals, especially women, without requiring collateral.
 
• Yunus's microfinance model has empowered millions of people to start small businesses and escape poverty.
 
• For his efforts, he was awarded the **Nobel Peace Prize** in 2006, along with Grameen Bank.
 
• His work has inspired microfinance initiatives worldwide, transforming the lives of countless individuals.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Amartya Sen:**

 
 
• **Amartya Sen** is a renowned economist and philosopher, known for his work on welfare economics and development theory.
 
• He was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences** in 1998 for his contributions to welfare economics and social choice theory.
 
• Sen's research focuses on issues like poverty, inequality, and human development, but he is not associated with microfinance.
 
• His concept of the **Human Development Index (HDI)** has been influential in measuring and improving quality of life globally.
 
• While Sen's work is impactful, he is not known as the Father of Microfinance.
 
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi:**
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** was a leader of India's independence movement and a global icon of nonviolent resistance.
 
• He advocated for self-reliance, rural development, and economic equality, but he did not establish microfinance institutions.
 
• Gandhi's principles inspired many social and economic reforms, but he is not directly linked to microfinance.
 
• His focus was on empowering communities through self-sufficiency and moral values.
 
• Gandhi's legacy is immense, but he is not recognized as the Father of Microfinance.
 
 
 
• **Mahbub Haq:**
 
 
• **Mahbub ul Haq** was a Pakistani economist known for his contributions to development economics and human development.
 
• He played a key role in creating the **Human Development Index (HDI)** alongside Amartya Sen.
 
• Haq's work emphasized reducing poverty and inequality, but he did not establish microfinance institutions.
 
• He served in various international organizations, including the World Bank and UNDP, advocating for sustainable development.
